Hi Monica / Marissa,

Thanks for the onboarding checklist — attaching our current COI and a roster of subcontractors who may do field install work on customer sites. Two quick questions from our broker:

1) Does Redwood require an Additional Insured endorsement that specifically names Redwood Inference *and* its subcontractors, or is naming Redwood alone sufficient?
2) For the waiver of subrogation, does Redwood accept a waiver only as to Redwood, or do you require it extended to all downstream subcontractors?

We want to avoid repeated endorsements for each subcontractor if not necessary. Weve attached: BespokeAI_COI.pdf, Subcontractor_Roster.xlsx.

Subject: RE: Vendor onboarding: COI and subcontractor coverage

Hi Samir — thanks for sending these over. Quick answers and next steps below.

Short answer: we need Additional Insured (AI) coverage that covers Redwood Inference and a single endorsement that explicitly covers work performed by your subcontractors. In practice we accept either: an AI endorsement naming "Redwood Inference, Inc. and its subsidiaries and affiliates" *plus* a subcontractor endorsement clause, or an AI that names Redwood and a separate blanket subcontractor endorsement covering all listed subs.

On waiver of subrogation: we require a waiver in favor of Redwood for liabilities arising out of subcontractor work on Redwood engagements. Extending the waiver to every downstream subcontractor is preferred but not mandatory if your insurer provides a blanket subcontractor waiver.

Procurement note: PO 764322 is on hold until we receive an endorsement that maps to the COI and names Redwood. If you can provide the insurers endorsement text or an updated COI with endorsements by EOD Friday (2027-06-25), procurement can release a conditional PO with standard hold language. See attached vendor_insurance_checklist.pdf for exact wording were requiring.

Action items:
- BespokeAI: request endorsement language from carrier and provide either updated COI + endorsement PDF or endorsement text (by 2027-06-25).
- Procurement (Marissa): prepare conditional PO template to release once endorsement is validated.
- Legal (Markus): confirm acceptable phrasing for conditional release and whether we need a performance bond for this engagement.

If you want, we can schedule a 15-min call tomorrow to walk through the endorsement wording with your broker.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Procurement Specialist
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: vendor_insurance_checklist.pdf)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Vendor onboarding: COI and subcontractor coverage

Monica — thanks. From a legal perspective, the shortest acceptable endorsement language were looking for is: 

"The insurance afforded by this policy shall also apply to liability arising out of work performed by subcontractors of the named insured, and Redwood Inference, Inc. is named as an Additional Insured with respect to liability arising out of the operations of the named insured."

For the waiver of subrogation: the insurers endorsement should include a waiver in favor of Redwood for claims arising out of subcontractor performance. If carrier cannot provide a single blanket waiver covering all subs, ask them to confirm the mechanism they will use (blanket wording vs. individual endorsements).

On the PO hold: Legal is comfortable with a conditional PO that contains explicit release conditions: (1) receipt of endorsed COI matching the policy limits on file, and (2) a representation that subcontractor roster is current at time of shipment/installation. No additional performance bond required at this stage; we can revisit if subs are not properly disclosed.

-Markus
Markus Klein
